name: IL-12
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+22 partisan lean anchors the race firmly Republican
Incumbent Mike Bost holds a massive financial edge ($1.3M raised vs. $88K for Fortier)
Prediction markets price Bost at roughly 96% to win
No public polling or expert ratings, but no evidence of a competitive race
model.rationale: The R+22 district lean, Bost's incumbency and roughly 15-to-1 fundraising advantage, and markets pricing his win probability near 96% all point the same direction, with no polling or headlines suggesting movement. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-based margin of about 19 points Republican.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing Fortier within single digits, or significant outside spending entering the district, would be the first sign this race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Bost seeks another term in a southern Illinois district that leans heavily Republican, about 22 points toward the GOP at the baseline. He was renominated without difficulty and enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised roughly $1.3 million and holding about $790,000 on hand. Democrat Julie Fortier has raised under $90,000 with no outside support on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, and prediction markets give Bost roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. With the incumbent's structural advantages and no evidence of a competitive contest, the district remains firmly in Republican hands, with the main uncertainty limited to the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
